full_parsed_record.title: Hikita probability lower-bound conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{E}_n$, let $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $T\in\operatorname{HikSYT}(\mathbf{m},\lambda)$. For the recursively defined Hikita weight $h_T(q)$ and every real $\alpha\geq0$, **Hikita probability lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
h_T(\alpha)\geq\frac{1}{\prod_i[\lambda_i]_{q=\alpha}!}.
$$

The source explains that this pointwise estimate would imply a lower bound for the specialized elementary coefficient and is not established there.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Isaiah Siegl, “Toward Lower Bounds for Chromatic Symmetric Functions in the Elementary Basis”, arXiv:2509.02841 (2026).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02841

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: The projective-rank lower bound for graph energy
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\xi_f(G)$ denote the projective rank of $G$. **Projective-rank energy conjecture.**

$$
\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{E}(G) \geq n-\xi_f(\overline{G}).
$$

This is proposed as a weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph energy conjecture and is motivated by the paper's semidefinite-programming lower bound involving the fractional chromatic number. The source presents it as a future research direction and gives no resolution.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Aida Abiad, Gabriel Coutinho, Emanuel Juliano and Luuk Reijnders, “A graph energy conjecture through the lenses of semidefinite programming”, arXiv:2509.05814 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05814

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Near-sharp sphere-counting conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $S(n,d)$ denote the number of $(d+2)$-tuples of points in $[n]^d$ that lie in a $(d-1)$-dimensional sphere. **Sphere-counting conjecture.** For any integer $d\geqslant 2$,

$$
S(n,d)=O\left(n^{d^2+d-1}\right).
$$

This conjecture would give an upper bound close to the lower bound in the paper's sphere-counting theorem. The paper's current upper bound leaves a gap, so this stronger estimate remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Anubhab Ghosal, Ritesh Goenka and Peter Keevash, “On subsets of lattice cubes avoiding affine and spherical degeneracies”, arXiv:2509.06935 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06935

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2025). “However, Lefmann refuted their conjecture for most values of $k$ and $d$ by showing that $f_{\mathrm{lin}}(n, d, k, k+1) = O(n^{d/\lceil k/2 \rceil})$.”

full_parsed_record.title: The first–second Zagreb index comparison conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$, edge set $E(G)$, order $n(G)$, size $m(G)$, vertex degree $d_G(v)$, first Zagreb index

$$
M_1(G)=\sum_{v\in V(G)}d_G(v)^2,
$$

and second Zagreb index

$$
M_2(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}d_G(u)d_G(v).
$$

**Zagreb index comparison conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected graph, then

$$
\frac{M_1(G)}{n(G)}\leq\frac{M_2(G)}{m(G)}.
$$

The conjecture arose in the study of graph-based descriptors of molecular structure. It is disproved for both general connected and disconnected graphs, although it is true for trees.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Ali Ghalavand, “On a Conjecture about Comparing the First and Second Zagreb Indices of Graphs”, arXiv:2509.07434 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07434

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: The common-difference set conjecture for cyclic arithmetic progressions
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $m,n,k\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ with $m>n$ and $nk\geq 3$. For subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_{mk}$ containing no $nk$-term cyclic arithmetic progression modulo $mk$, let $D(mk,nk)$ denote the set of common differences that need to be considered.

**Common-difference set conjecture.**

$$
D(mk,nk)=\{1\leq g\leq m:g\mid nk\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes the analogue of the paper's earlier description of relevant common differences for the more general case where the progression length $nk$ shares a common factor with the modulus $mk$. Establishing it could support bounds for chromatic numbers $\chi(mk,nk)$ and independence numbers of cyclic Van der Waerden hypergraphs $H_{mk,nk}$, although such generalizations do not directly improve the bounds for $W_c(k,r)$.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Benjamin Liber, “On the Independence Numbers of the Cyclic Van der Waerden Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2509.07926 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Lejeune–Rigo–Rosenfeld conjecture on Arnoux–Rauzy words
full_parsed_record.statement: Let $w$ be an Arnoux–Rauzy infinite word. Its $2$-binomial complexity and subword complexity are functions assigning to each positive integer the number of equivalence classes of factors of that length under, respectively, $2$-binomial equivalence and equality. **Lejeune–Rigo–Rosenfeld conjecture.** The $2$-binomial complexity of $w$ coincides with its subword complexity. This generalizes the corresponding property known for Sturmian words; apart from the Sturmian and eventually constant cases, the Tribonacci word is the principal known example, and the conjecture remains open in general.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Léo Vivion, “New examples of words for which binomial complexities and subword complexity coincide”, arXiv:2509.11172 (2026).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11172

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2025). “Since Arnoux-Rauzy words are themselves a generalization of Sturmian words, this raises the following open questions.”

full_parsed_record.title: Facet adjacency conjecture for concordancy classes
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $u\in W_c^+$, let $\mathsf{CC}_c(u)$ be the concordancy poset, and let $\Delta(\mathcal{C})$ denote the collection of SBDW simplices associated with a class $\mathcal{C}$. **Facet-adjacency conjecture.** Two distinct classes $\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}'\in\mathsf{CC}_c(u)$ are adjacent in the Hasse diagram of $\leq_\Delta$ if and only if an SBDW simplex in

$$
\{\operatorname{conv}(u\vec{\pi}\mathfrak{y}):\vec{\pi}\in\mathcal{C}\}
$$

shares a facet with an SBDW simplex in

$$
\{\operatorname{conv}(u\vec{\pi}\mathfrak{y}):\vec{\pi}\in\mathcal{C}'\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a geometric characterization of adjacency in the concordancy poset; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Colin Defant, Melissa Sherman-Bennett and Nathan Williams, “Permutahedron Triangulations via Total Linear Stability and the Dual Braid Group”, arXiv:2509.11497 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11497

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Lattice conjecture for the c-noncrossing weak order
full_parsed_record.statement: Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group and let $c$ be a Coxeter element. The **$c$-noncrossing weak order** on $W$ is the poset obtained by restricting the Cayley graph of the dual braid monoid to the interval corresponding to $W$. **Williams's lattice conjecture.** The $c$-noncrossing weak order on $W$ is a lattice. This is one of the proposed future directions for the new order; the supplied text gives no general proof.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Colin Defant, Melissa Sherman-Bennett and Nathan Williams, “Permutahedron Triangulations via Total Linear Stability and the Dual Braid Group”, arXiv:2509.11497 (2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Lattice conjecture for the c-noncrossing Bruhat order
full_parsed_record.statement: Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group and let $c$ be a Coxeter element. The **$c$-noncrossing Bruhat order** is the order on $W$ defined from the noncrossing Bruhat construction. **Bruhat-order lattice conjecture.** The $c$-noncrossing Bruhat order on $W$ is a lattice. Together with the proposed isomorphism to the c-noncrossing weak order, this would be equivalent to the corresponding weak-order lattice conjecture; the supplied text gives no general proof.

full_parsed_record.title: The direct-product conjecture for clean graphs over rings
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $R_1$, $R_2$, $P_1$, and $P_2$ be rings such that

$$
Cl_2(R_1)\cong Cl_2(R_2)
$$

and

$$
P_1\cong P_2.
$$

**Direct-product conjecture.** The clean graphs satisfy

$$
Cl_2(R_1\times P_1)\cong Cl_2(R_2\times P_2).
$$

This conjecture proposes that isomorphic clean graphs are preserved when taking direct products with isomorphic rings. The supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence beyond its derivation as a generalization of the preceding theorem.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Felicia Servina Djuang, Indah Emilia Wijayanti and Yeni Susanti, “Isomorphism of Clean Graphs over Z_n and Structural Insight into M_2(Z_p)”, arXiv:2509.12004 (2025).

full_parsed_record.title: The endpoint monotonicity conjecture for polygonal lines of combinatorial Petrie matrices
full_parsed_record.statement: Let $A\in \mathcal{CP}(n)$ and let $L$ be its corresponding polygonal line. If $n$ is even, consider the endpoints of $L$ ordered by increasing $x$-coordinate. **Endpoint monotonicity conjecture.** Their $y$-coordinates are weakly increasing in that order. The polygonal line is associated with a combinatorial Petrie matrix, and the claim concerns an additional monotonicity property beyond the established non-self-intersection and closed-curve properties. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.

full_parsed_record.title: Meunier's stability conjecture for stable Kneser hypergraphs
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathrm{KG}^r(n,k)_{s\textup{-stab}}$ be the induced $r$-uniform Kneser hypergraph whose vertices are the $s$-stable $k$-subsets of $[n]$, where $s$-stability means $s\leq|i-j|\leq n-s$ for distinct elements $i,j$. **Meunier's conjecture.** If $r,s\geq2$ and $n\geq\max\{r,s\}k$, then

$$
\chi\left(\mathrm{KG}^r(n,k)_{s\textup{-stab}}\right)=\left\lceil\frac{n-\max\{r,s\}(k-1)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

This extends Ziegler's conjecture from $r$-stable to $s$-stable Kneser hypergraphs. The source does not specify the general resolution status; it also notes that an alternative generalization was later found incorrect.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Hamid Reza Daneshpajouh, “On the Chromatic Number of Stable Kneser Hypergraphs: Verifying the Conjecture for New Families”, arXiv:2509.22026 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22026

full_parsed_record.title: Barycentric subdivision conjecture for exterior algebraic shifting of surfaces
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $K$ be a surface triangulation, let $\operatorname{sd}(K)$ denote its barycentric subdivision, and let $\Delta^{ex}$ denote exterior algebraic shifting over a fixed field. A homology lex-segment is a simplicial complex whose faces form the corresponding homology lex-segment.

**Barycentric subdivision conjecture.** If $K$ is a surface triangulation, then $\Delta^{ex}(\operatorname{sd}(K))$ is a homology lex-segment.

This is proposed as the surface analogue of the deterministic statement known for barycentric subdivisions of graphs. It would provide a possible route toward the conjectured concentration result for uniform triangulations of fixed surfaces; the source gives no resolution.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Denys Bulavka, Eran Nevo and Yuval Peled, “The typical algebraic shifting of a surface”, arXiv:2509.26525 (2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Antisymmetry conjecture for the matching preorder
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the set of labelled perfect matchings, equipped with the preorder $\preceq$. **Antisymmetry conjecture.** The preorder $(\mathcal{M}_n,\preceq)$ is a poset; equivalently,

$$
M\preceq N\text{ and }N\preceq M\quad\Longrightarrow\quad M=N.
$$

The paper presents this as a consequence that would follow from the switch-generation conjecture, and the supplied parser gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Joseph Briggs, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “Degree sequences realizing labelled perfect matchings”, arXiv:2510.01110 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01110

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “This conjecture is open in general; see Shook for a discussion of partial results.”

full_parsed_record.title: Upper bound for outer general position number after vertex removal
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $x$ be a vertex that is not a cut vertex of $G$. Write ${\rm gp}_{\rm o}(G)$ for the outer general position number of $G$ and $\deg_G(x)$ for the degree of $x$ in $G$. **Upper-bound conjecture.** If $x$ is not a cut vertex of $G$, then

$$
{\rm gp}_{\rm o}(G-x) \le {\rm gp}_{\rm o}(G) + \deg_G(x).
$$

This would provide a general upper bound for the change in outer general position number under deletion of a non-cut vertex. Together with the preceding lower-bound theorem for vertices lying in an outer general position set, it would constrain how vertex removal affects ${\rm gp}_{\rm o}(G)$; the supplied text does not indicate whether the proposed bound is known or remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Jing Tian, Pakanun Dokyeesun and Sandi Klavžar, “On the variety of general position problems under vertex and edge removal”, arXiv:2510.01294 (2026).
full_parsed_record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Beck–Brauner–? conjecture for $q,t$-symmetry of $(a,b,\ldots,b)$-Dyck paths
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\vec{k}$ be a vector of positive integers and define the area-bounce polynomial

$$
C_{\vec{k}}(q,t)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{D}_{\vec{k}}}q^{\mathrm{area}(\pi)}t^{\mathrm{bounce}(\pi)}.
$$

A polynomial is $q,t$-symmetric when $F(q,t)=F(t,q)$. **The $(a,b,\ldots,b)$-symmetry conjecture.** For any positive integers $a$ and $b$, if

$$
\vec{k}=(a,b,b,\ldots,b),
$$

then

$$
C_{\vec{k}}(q,t)=C_{\vec{k}}(t,q).
$$

The conjecture is attributed in the paper to the authors of the cited polyhedral-geometry work. The cited work proposes this family, while the supplied excerpt gives no proof or later resolution.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Menghao Qu and Yingrui Zhang, “Symmetry of the refined q,t-Catalan polynomials for k-Dyck paths”, arXiv:2510.08196 (2026).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08196

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “However, a combinatorial proof of these $q,t$-symmetries remains an open problem.”

full_parsed_record.title: Isospectrality conjecture for generalized projective graphs over finite local rings
full_parsed_record.statement: Let $p$, $r$, and $d$ be as above, and let $2\leq m<n\leq d$. full_parsed_record.title: Elsholtz–Rackham counting conjecture for higher-dimensional grids
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $[n]^d$ carry coordinatewise addition, and let $k_d$ be the maximal volume of a region in the unit cube $[0,1]^d$ bounded between a hyperplane $H$ and its dilate $2\cdot H$.

**Elsholtz–Rackham's higher-dimensional conjecture.** The number of sum-free subsets of $[n]^d$ is

$$
2^{k_dn^d+O_d(n^{d-1})}.
$$

This extends the two-dimensional counting conjecture using the extremal constant $k_d$. The supplied text does not state a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Anubhab Ghosal, “On the number of sum-free subsets of the square grid”, arXiv:2510.15621 (2025).

full_parsed_record.title: The independence-number lower-bound conjecture for log-concavity failures
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $N$ vertices, with independence sequence $(a_i)$ and independence number $\alpha(T)$. **Independence-number lower-bound conjecture.** If the independence sequence is not log-concave at index $N/2-\beta$, then

$$
\alpha(T)\geq N/2+\beta+1.
$$

This claim describes a necessary separation between the location of a log-concavity failure and the tree's independence number. The supplied text presents it as a conjectural principle, but does not state whether it has been resolved.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Eric Ramos and Sunny Sun, “An AI enhanced approach to the tree unimodality conjecture”, arXiv:2510.18826 (2025).

full_parsed_record.title: Jeffs's convexity conjecture for neural codes with four maximal codewords
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a neural code, meaning a collection of subsets of a neuron set, and call a codeword **maximal** if it is not properly contained in another codeword. A code is **convex** if it can be realized as the code of a collection of convex open sets in Euclidean space. A **local obstruction** and a **wheel** are the combinatorial obstructions described in the source.

**Jeffs's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ has up to four maximal codewords, then $\mathcal{C}$ is convex if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ has no local obstructions and no wheels.

This conjecture extends the known characterization for codes with at most six neurons and four maximal codewords, where convexity is equivalent to avoiding local obstructions and wheels. Its status is not specified in the source.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Saber Ahmed, Natasha Crepeau, Gisel Flores, Osiano Isekenegbe, Deanna Perez and Anne Shiu, “Convexity of Neural Codes with Four Maximal Codewords”, arXiv:2510.20323 (2025).
